title: Everything wrong with Online Masculinity and Modern Bodybuilding all in one meat
summary: NH takes apart Liver King's nine 'ancestral tenets' (sleep, eat, move, shield, connect, cold, sun, fight, bond). He argues each tenet is sensible on the surface but serves as a marketing funnel for supplements, sold on a drug-built physique to young men in a masculinity crisis. He uses it as a case study of grifting in the fitness industry and of fake online masculinity.
claims: Every six months a new jacked grifter appears, builds an audience, makes money and disappears; that is what modern bodybuilding produces
Natty-or-not videos are stupid speculation that harms viewers and gives the target free publicity that drives traffic to their products
Steroid-using influencers typically go through a phase of denying it that can last their whole life
Grifters' tenets are deliberately sensible (sleep, whole food, sun, training) so you trust them; the trap is the product that comes afterwards
Liver King's sleep advice leads to buying blue-light glasses, and googling his name surfaces supplements first, whereas NH's name surfaces a free program
Men lacking role models, fathers or contact with nature are the target of hyper-masculine personas that end up selling them products
It is an inversion of values for men clearly on exogenous hormones to be presented as the model of how to be a man
Organ meats are not unhealthy and have some benefit, but eating them for size is a 60-70 year old gimmick and no food has the power to make you big
A raw-meat diet is not balanced, most people shouldn't eat like that, and raw meat risks bacterial illness
Eating meat bought at a supermarket doesn't make you masculine
The funnel is a hard 'ancestral' habit first, then a pricier, easier supplement version of it, because everyone prefers the path of least resistance
Grifters who are on drugs can't give methods that work, so they keep ready-made excuses (bad technique, genetics, effort) when followers fail
Experienced lifters see through bearded 'natural' personas; their followers tend to be beginners with little muscle of their own
Liver King's base training resembles a modified Westside barbell system, good for strength and usable for size
The carcass carries, weighted-vest hikes and sled drags he promotes are about 5% of his training and not very effective for hypertrophy
You cannot sell the basics: compound plus isolation movements are the best way for a natural to train but have no marketing appeal
Bodybuilding's glorification of pain and puke-bucket workouts is pointless; growth requires discipline and sensible movements for many years
You cannot shock the muscle; switch exercises for boredom or injury avoidance, not for growth
Good information is nearly useless commercially; packaging and entertainment are what sell
Big naturals with 10+ years of training have average to above-average testosterone, nothing supraphysiological; the difference is training time
Fixing your hormonal profile is only the first step; after that you have to train
Evolution is driven by shortcuts; trying to return to caveman days, as Nietzsche predicted of men in a crisis of modernity, is impossible
Grounding/barefoot walking won't grow muscle or undo cardiovascular damage from steroid use
Normies overestimate object weights: a fridge is about 50 lb, a pressed branch perhaps 40 lb, roughly an empty barbell
NH trains in a gym at about 20°F for eight months a year; the cold gives small benefits but large disadvantages and he wouldn't recommend it
Cold exposure won't make you jacked; seeking discomfort builds the toughness to stick to training for years, which is what builds the body
A constant red flush on the chest and arms in enhanced lifters signals high blood pressure/red blood cell elevation and health risk
Bodybuilding won't make you a fighter; if you want combat ability, do MMA or boxing
Worshipping and following a man is the opposite of masculinity, which is the ability to stand by yourself and develop your own identity
Masculinity is free; buying products and worshipping people is not masculine
The skinny followers of guru lifestyles never attain the physique that sells it, proving the physique comes from drugs, not the method
